name: Slack
headline: Moderate: you can ship to any workspace without review, but unlisted apps get a harsh 1 request per minute on conversations.history, so reading channels at scale effectively needs Marketplace approval.

firstTest.text: About 15 minutes. Create an app at api.slack.com/apps, add scopes, add an HTTPS redirect URL, and install it to your own workspace.

production.text: Unlisted path: same day. Activate Public Distribution and any workspace can install via the Add to Slack button. Marketplace path: needs 10 active workspaces first, then weeks of review.

approvalWait.text: None for unlisted distribution. Marketplace: preliminary review up to 10 business days, functional review up to 10 weeks for new submissions.

whoCanRegister.text: Anyone with a Slack account can create an app. To go beyond one workspace, finish the Manage Distribution checklist and click Activate Public Distribution. Workspace admins may need to approve installs.

testMode.text: A single-workspace app works with no limits from distribution. Once distributed without Marketplace approval, new installs get conversations.history and conversations.replies at 1 request per minute with a max of 15 objects. If you turn on token rotation, access tokens last 12 hours.

actions.label: Send messages
actions.review: None for unlisted. The scope page gives no review note.

actions.label: Read public channel history
actions.review: No review to install. Unlisted apps are rate-limited to 1 request per minute on this method.

actions.label: Read private channels and DMs
actions.review: Broad data access scopes are questioned in Marketplace review. Same rate limit applies if unlisted.
actions.timeToLive: same day unlisted; weeks if listing

actions.label: Post as the user
actions.review: None for unlisted. Requested with user_scope, not scope.

steps.title: Create the app
steps.detail: Go to api.slack.com/apps, choose Create New App, pick your dev workspace.

steps.title: Add scopes
steps.detail: OAuth & Permissions. Bot scopes go in scope. Per-user scopes go in user_scope. Ask for the minimum: admins read the permission list before approving.

steps.title: Add HTTPS redirect URL
steps.detail: Add your callback under OAuth & Permissions > Redirect URLs. It must be https. The redirect_uri you send must match it. No # anchors.

steps.title: Build the OAuth flow
steps.detail: Send users to the authorize URL with state. Exchange the code (valid 10 minutes) with oauth.v2.access. Store the bot token (xoxb-) and any user token (xoxp-) per workspace.

steps.title: Decide on token rotation
steps.detail: Opt-in. Access tokens then last 12 hours and refresh tokens are single use. You cannot turn it off later. Bolt SDKs handle it.

steps.title: Meet distribution requirements
steps.detail: HTTPS on redirect, events, and interactivity URLs. Plan onboarding, since you can't hand-hold every workspace.

steps.title: Activate Public Distribution
steps.detail: Manage Distribution > Share Your App with Other Workspaces > finish the checklist > Activate Public Distribution. You get an Add to Slack button and an install URL.

steps.title: Plan around the rate limit
steps.detail: Unlisted apps: conversations.history and conversations.replies at 1 request per minute, limit capped at 15. Use Events API pushes or webhooks instead of polling history.

steps.title: Optional: Marketplace review
steps.detail: Needs 10 active workspaces (28 days), a privacy policy, support within 2 business days, and scope justifications. Preliminary review up to 10 business days; functional review up to 10 weeks.

blockers.title: 1 request per minute on conversations.history
blockers.fix: Applies to new unlisted commercial apps and new installs after 29 May 2025. Marketplace approval removes it. Existing installs and internal customer-built apps are exempt. Design for event pushes, not history polling.

blockers.title: Cannot submit to Marketplace yet
blockers.fix: Slack wants at least 10 active workspaces (used in the last 28 days) before you can submit. Run as unlisted first.

blockers.title: Workspace admin approval
blockers.fix: Some workspaces require admin approval of installs, and admins judge the scopes. Keep scopes minimal and explain each one.

blockers.title: http redirect rejected
blockers.fix: Redirect URLs and redirect_uri must be https. No localhost exception is documented. Use an https tunnel in development.

blockers.title: Rotation cannot be undone
blockers.fix: Once token rotation is on it can't be turned off. Build refresh and save the new refresh token on every refresh.

blockers.title: Marketplace rejects broad scopes
blockers.fix: Legacy or restricted scopes and scopes giving broad workspace data access are not accepted. Justify each scope in writing.

agentCan: Write the OAuth install flow with state and per-workspace token storage
Replace history polling with Events API handlers
Draft scope justifications for Marketplace review
youDo: Create the app under your Slack account
Provide a privacy policy and a support channel
Supply a test account and optional demo video for review
Workspace admins at customers approve installs where required

drafts.title: App description
drafts.body: [Product] connects your AI assistant to Slack. It posts messages you ask for and reads the channels you add it to. It never reads channels it is not invited to.

drafts.title: Scope justification for review
drafts.body: chat:write: send messages the user asks the assistant to send. channels:history: read messages in channels where the app is installed so it can answer questions about them. We do not store message text beyond [N days].

drafts.title: Message for a workspace admin
drafts.body: We'd like to install [Product] in our Slack. It requests: [list scopes in plain words]. It only reads channels it is invited to. Install link: [Add to Slack URL].
